court: In the High Court of Madras
judges_raw: (Before Anita Sumanth and Sunder Mohan, JJ.)
respondents: Addl. Chief Secretary to the Government, Home Prohibition & Excise (XVI) Department and Others

prayer: Prayer: Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India praying to issue to writ of habeas corpus to call for the entire records connected with the detention order in Rc. No. 691/2025/M6, D. No. 30/2025 on 14-8-2025 on the file of the 2nd respondent and quash the same and direct the respondents to produce the petitioner's son Manikandan, S/o. judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

Sunder Mohan, J.:— The father of the detenu one Manikandan has filed this writ petition challenging the detention order dated 14-8-2025 passed against his son and branding his as Drug Offender under Section 2(e) of the Tamil Nadu Preventive Detention Act, 1982 (Act).

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the detenu had not filed any bail application and that the detaining authority had relied upon an order passed in Crl.M.P. No. 3109 of 2021 to conclude that the detenue is likely to be released on bail; that the said facts in that case are not similar; and that consequently, the conclusion of the detaining authority that the detenu is likely to file a bail application and be released on bail, suffers from non-application of mind.

3. Heard the learned Additional Public Prosecutor.

4. It is seen from the grounds of detention that the detaining authority had relied upon an order passed in Crl.M.P. No. 3109 of 2021 dated 29-10-2025 to conclude that the detenu is likely to be released on bail, when he moves a bail application. However, the facts of that case are not similar to the facts in the instant case. The detenu has two previous cases under the NDPS Act whereas the accused in Crl.M.P. No. 3109 of 2021 had no previous cases. Therefore, this Court is of the view that the satisfaction of the detaining authority that the detenu likely to be released on bail by placing reliance on the said order is misconceived. Since the order suffers from non-application of mind, we are inclined to set aside the impugned order.

5. In light of the aforesaid, this Habeas Corpus Petition is allowed and the Detention Order passed by the second respondent in Rc. No. 691/2025/M6, D. No. 30/2025 dated 14-8-2025 is set aside.

6. The detenu viz. Manikandan, S/o. Dhatchanamoorthi, aged 28 years, now confined in Central Prison, Puzhal, Chennai - 600 066, is directed to be set at liberty forthwith, unless his presence is required in connection with any other case.
